title: Cost & Latency Signal Federator — per-route/model/customer tally engine
creator: Marcus Chen
description: Deliver a robust 'Signal Federator' service that normalizes and tallies cost and latency signals across routes, model variants, and customers. The federator consumes telemetry from runtime logs, billing events, and routing decisions to produce a single canonical per-route/per-model/per-customer breakdown used by Console cost dashboards and downstream billing reconciliations.
background: Our current console pipelines emit multiple partially-overlapping economic signals (runtime token counts, GPU time samples, per-request latency spans, routing fallbacks). These signals are processed by ad-hoc jobs and produce inconsistent per-route and per-customer numbers that complicate SLAs and chargeback. This ticket scopes a single service to unify, normalize, and attribute those signals with deterministic rules and clear lineage.
success_criteria: 1) The federator produces a daily canonical breakdown file for all active routes with per-model and per-customer slices within SLO windows. 2) Console dashboards adopt the federated output and show <=2% variance from gold-standard spot checks. 3) Billing reconciliation jobs ingest federated outputs with no manual fixes needed for a full billing cycle. 4) End-to-end latency for federator ingestion to availability is <= 30 minutes for streaming mode and <= 4 hours for backfill mode.
architecture_overview: The federator is a stateless service with a checkpointed ingestion layer. It exposes a protobuf-based ingestion API and reads batch blobs from the telemetry lake. Core components: (a) normalizer to map disparate event schemas to the canonical signal model, (b) attribution engine to apportion cost/latency across route/model/customer using deterministic weights, (c) combiner to merge per-shard tallies and emit time-windowed outputs, (d) lineage metadata writer that tags outputs with source keys and confidence scores.
data_sources:
- Runtime telemetry (kafka: runtime-spans, runtime-metrics)
- Billing meter events (s3: billing/charges/day/)
- Routing decisions (kafka: route-decisions)
- Model catalog (internal: models service snapshot)
- Customer metadata (internal: tenant registry)
- Cached KV hits/explicit prefix-cache entries (bigtable snapshot)
pipeline_stages:
1) Ingest: stream + batch connectors normalize event timestamps and align to ingestion windows.
2) Enrich: join events with model and tenant metadata; expand route path templates to canonical route ids.
3) Weighting: apply deterministic allocation rules (token-based default, GPU-time override when available, latency-proportional apportion for shared resources).
4) Combine: reduce per-window partials with idempotent merge semantics.
5) Emit: write canonical CSV/Parquet to analytics-prod/federated-breakdowns/YYYY-MM-DD and publish completion event.
6) Lineage & QC: compute confidence score, attach anomaly flags, persist QC artifacts to data-quality bucket.
output_schema: Fields: date, window_start, window_end, route_id, model_id, customer_id, total_tokens, total_gpu_ms, total_request_count, avg_p99_latency_ms, cost_usd, allocation_reason, confidence_score, source_keys (list), computed_at
api_contracts:
- Ingest API (gRPC): IngestSignal(Stream<NormalizedEvent>) returns IngestAck.
- Query API (REST): GET /federator/v1/breakdown?date=YYYY-MM-DD&route=... returns precomputed slice (JSON).
- Health API: /healthz and /metrics (Prometheus).
- Event: federator.completion.v1 published to kafka when daily file is ready.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): run in shadow mode for 2 weeks ingesting 10% of traffic and emit federated outputs to staging.
Phase 2 (parallel): feed outputs into Console read path behind feature flag for synthetic customers.
Phase 3 (switch): enable default Console dashboards to read federated outputs and monitor discrepancy dashboards for 7 days.
Rollback: revert console read path to legacy aggregates; drop feature flag.
monitoring_slo:
- Availability: 99.95% for ingestion and combine services.
- Freshness: streaming slices available within 30 minutes 99% of the time.
- Accuracy: automated spot-check comparisons against gold standard must be within 2% for token/cost totals.
- Error budget alerts: trigger on sustained 5-minute error rate > 1%.
testing_plan: Unit tests for normalization and weighting rules, integration tests using synthetic traces and billing events, nightly full-scan backfill against prior month to validate parity, and load test to validate peak throughput (target: 1M events/min sustained, 5M events/min burst). Include chaos tests for partial kafka partition loss and schema evolution.
migration_strategy: Run federator in parallel and store outputs with version tags. For the first billing cycle, surface federated outputs as 'preview' in Console while continuing to write legacy aggregates. After 2 successful cycles with no reconciliation edits, mark federated outputs as authoritative and retire legacy job. Keep historical mapping table for at least 180 days.
security_privacy: Federator must redact PII from route metadata. Access to outputs requires analytics:read role. Outputs stored in s3 are encrypted with customer-managed KMS per tenant where required. security_review_required: true
risk_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Double-counting when events cross time windows. Mitigation: use deterministic windowing and idempotent merge keys.
- Risk: Model metadata drift causing mis-attribution. Mitigation: snapshot model catalog per-run and validate model_id hashes.
- Risk: Performance regressions under heavy backfill. Mitigation: backfill throttle and separate compute tier.
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end pipeline runs on canary dataset and produces expected schema with confidence > 0.9.
2) Console shows federated breakdown for selected customers and teams confirm numbers by manual spot checks.
3) No unresolved data-quality flags for 3 consecutive days.
4) Security review completed and KMS integration verified.
stakeholders: PM: Jonah Keene, Eng Lead: Lena Ortiz, Data Eng: Priya Nandan, Observability: Eric Zhao, Billing Ops: Sofia Martinez
notes: Implementation should favor immutability of outputs and include an easy replay key. Consider adding a lightweight UI for analysts to re-run a federator job for a given date-range with debug verbosity. Keep the allocation rules configurable via feature flags and expose weights for per-tenant overrides.
